reading-the-signpost-at-the-centre-of-ca.text: If the player reads the signpost:

steps.prompt: Start the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest?

steps.text: The signpost has a note pinned onto it. The note says:'----Braindead Butler Wanted----Gravedigging skills essential - Hunchback advantageousSee Dr Fenkenstrain at the castle NE of Canifis'
You've started a new quest: Creature of Fenkenstrain

dr-fenkenstrain-attempting-to-pickpocket.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
dr-fenkenstrain-attempting-to-pickpocket.text: What do you think you're doing???

dr-fenkenstrain-talking-to-dr-fenkenstra.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
dr-fenkenstrain-talking-to-dr-fenkenstra.text: Have you come to apply for the job?

steps.player: Yes, if it pays well.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I'll have to ask you some questions first.

steps.player: Okay...

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: How would you describe yourself in one word?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Mmmm, I see.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I don't think you have the aptitude for this position.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Mmmm, I see.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Just one more question. What would you say is your greatest skill?

steps.player: Combat.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Mmmm, I see.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I don't think you have the aptitude for this position.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Mmmm, I see.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Looks like you're just the [man/woman] for the job! Welcome aboard!

steps.player: Is there anything you'd like me to do for you, sir?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Yes, there is. You're highly skilled at grave-digging, yes?

steps.player: Err...yes, that's what I said.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Excellent. Now listen carefully.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I need you to find some...stuff...for me.

steps.player: Stuff?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: That's what I said...stuff.

steps.player: What kind of stuff?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Well...dead stuff.

steps.player: Go on...

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I need you to get me enough dead body parts for me to stitch together a complete body, which I plan to bring to life.

steps.player: Right...okay...if you insist.
No thanks, I wouldn't work here if you paid me.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Charming.

options.text: Do you know where I could find body parts?

steps.player: Do you know where I could find body parts?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: The soil of Morytania is unique in its ability to preserve the bodies of the dead, which is one reason why I have chosen to carry out my experiments here.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I recommend digging up some graves in the local area. To the south-east you will find the Haunted Woods; I believe there are many graves there.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: There is also a mausoleum on an island west of this castle. I expect the bodies that are buried there to be extremely well preserved, as they were wealthy in life.

options.text: Remind me what you want me to do.

steps.player: What do you want me to do, again?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I need you to get me enough dead body parts for me to stitch together a complete body, which I plan to bring to life.

steps.player: Right...okay...if you insist.

options.text: Why are you trying to make this creature?

steps.player: Why do you want to make a creature?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I came to the land of Morytania many years ago, to find a safe sanctuary for my experiments. This abandoned castle suited my purposes exactly.

steps.player: What were you experimenting in?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Oh, perfectly innocent experiments - for the good of mankind.

steps.player: Then why did you need to come to Morytania?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Enough questions, now. Get back to your work.

options.text: Will this creature put me out of a job?

steps.player: Will this creature put me out of a job?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: No, my friend. I have a very special purpose in mind for this creature.

options.text: I must get back to work, sir.

steps.player: I must get back to work, sir.
Can you tell me anything about Fenkenstrain?

steps.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
The Headless Gardener's neck twitches at you, but the lack of any head prevents him from speaking.
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
You feel power emanate from the Amulet of Ghostspeak, and the air around you vibrates with the ghostly voice of the Headless Gardener...

steps.player: Can you tell me anything about Fenkenstrain?

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Oi could tell you a few things about old Fenky, yeah.

steps.player: Go on.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Once, this castle were full o' good folk - my friends. Fenky was just the castle doctor you know, to the Lord and the castle folk.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: I don't know what happened to them all, but one by one they all disappeared. When they were gone a while, I went an dug graves for 'em, in the forest.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: After a while there weren't no-one left, but the Lord, Fenkenstrain, and meself.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Old Fenky sent me into the Forest to dig 'im a pit. Never said what for. Then would you believe it, someone chops me head off.

steps.player: Did you see who did it, before ...

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Before oi kicked the bucket, you mean?

steps.player: Umm...

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Don't worry yourself, I'm not worried about bein' dead. Worse things could happen, I suppose.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: One thing I do know is, there ain't no Lord of the castle anymore, 'cept for old Fenky. Makes you think a bit, don't it?

steps.player: Can you tell me anything about Fenkenstrain?

steps.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
If the player is wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:
You feel power emanate from the Amulet of Ghostspeak, and the air around you vibrates with the ghostly voice of the Headless Gardener...

steps.player: What happened to your head?

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Oi was in the old 'aunted Forest to the south, diggin' a pit for moi old maaster, old Fenkenstrain, when would you believe it, someone chops me head off. Awful bad luck, weren't it?

steps.player: Oh yes, dreadful bad luck.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: So oi thinks to meself, I don't needs any 'ead to be gettin on with me gardenin', long as I got me hands and me spade.

steps.player: Would you show me where the place was?

steps.text: If the player already found the head:

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: No mate, you've found my head already, oi think.
If the player does not have the head:
The Gardener Ghost follows the player

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Well, oi s'pose oi've got 10 minutes to spare.

steps.player: Can you tell me anything about Fenkenstrain?

steps.text: If the player is not wearing the amulet of ghostspeak:

You feel power emanate from the Amulet of Ghostspeak, and the air around you vibrates with the ghostly voice of the Headless Gardener...

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Me name? It's been a moivellous long while, mate, since I had any use for such a thing as a name.

steps.player: Don't worry, I was just trying to make conversation.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: No, no, I can't be havin' that - I'll remember in a minute-

steps.player: Please, don't worry.

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: Lestwit, that's it! Ed Lestwit!

finding-the-torso-arms-and-legs-using-th.text: ...And who knows what problems will come up if we have an undead head on a truly dead body.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.text: If the player brought the needle and five thread to Dr Fenkenstrain:

steps.text: Fenkenstrain uses the needle and thread to sew the body parts together. Soon, a hideous creature lies inanimate on the ritual table.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Perfect. But I need one more thing from you - flesh and bones by themselves do not make life.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I have honed to perfection an ancient ritual that will give life to this creature, but for this I must harness the very power of Nature.

steps.player: And what power is this?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: The power of lightning.

steps.player: Sorry, can't make lightning, you've got the wrong man-

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Silence your insolent tongue! The storm that brews overhead will create the lightning. What I need you to do is to repair the lightning conductor on the balcony above.

steps.player: Repair the lightning conductor, right. Can I have a break, soon? By law I'm entitled to 15 minutes every-

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Repair the conductor and BEGONE!!!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.player: How do I repair the lightning conductor?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.text: Oh, it would be easier to do it myself! If you find a conductor mould you should be able to cast a new one.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-with-the-body.text: Remember this, [player name]: my experiment will only work with a conductor made from silver.

steps.player: Where is he now?

steps.speaker: Gardener Ghost
steps.text: E's dead, just like everyone else round 'ere ... 'cept for me.

steps.text: The lightning conductor is now beyond repair.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: Yes, I'm afraid it did, LogWarden - all too well.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: I tricked it into going up to the Tower, and there it remains, imprisoned.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.player: So the creature wasn't all you'd hoped, then?
Oh, I see, we're developing a sense of right and wrong now are we?
Bit late for that, I'd say.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: I have no control over it! It's coming to get me!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.player: What do you want me to do about it?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-after-using-t.text: Destroy it!!! Take the key to the Tower and take back the life I never should have granted!!!

talking-to-the-gardener-ghost-after-usin.speaker: Gardener Ghost
talking-to-the-gardener-ghost-after-usin.text: Same as ever, mate, just getting' on with it regardless.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I am commanded to destroy you, creature!
You really don't know, do you? Have a look for yourself.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: The creature stumbles over towards the mirror, focuses upon his reflection and...
The creature becomes instantly sober, horror all too evident in his undead eyes.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I'm sorry. I suppose I'm partly to blame for this.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: No - it was him I wager - Fenkenstrain - wasn't it? He's brought me back to life!

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: I was Rologarth, Lord of the North Coast - this castle was once mine. Fenkenstrain was the castle doctor.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: So the castle wasn't really abandoned when he found it?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Is that what he told you? No, no, this castle was once full of people and life. Fenkenstrain advised me to sell them to the vampyres, which - I am sad to say - I did.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I found your brain in a jar in Canifis, so he must have sold you too.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Of that I will not speak. There lie memories that should rest with the dead, the living unable to bear them.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: That's it - I'm leaving this dreadful place, whether I get paid or not. Is there anything I can do for you before I leave?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: Only one - please stop Fenkenstrain from carrying on his experiments, once and for all, so that no other poor soul has to endure suffering such as that of my people and I.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.player: Do you know how I can stop Fenkenstrain's experiments?

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: Take the Ring of Charos from him.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: It was my birthright, passed down to me through the ages, its origin forgotten.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: The Ring of Charos has many powers, but Fenkenstrain has bent them to his own evil purposes. Without the power of the ring, he will not be able to raise the dead from their sleep.

talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.speaker: Fenkenstrain's Monster
talking-to-the-creature-of-fenkenstrain-.text: It has one other, extremely important use - it confuses the werewolves' senses, making them believe that they smell one of their own kind. Without the ring, Fenkenstrain will be at their mercy.

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.player: Never, now that he has told me the truth!

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.text: Oh my, oh my, this is exactly what I feared!

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.text: Why did you have to pick Rologarth's brain of all brains?!?

convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
convincing-dr-fenkenstrain-to-stop-his-e.text: No!! I refuse to release you!! You must help me build another creature to destroy this dreadful mistake!!
If the player pickpockets Dr Fenkenstrain:

steps.text: You steal the Ring of Charos from Fenkenstrain.
1000 Thieving experience
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: Creature of Fenkenstrain

post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.player: I stole the Ring of Charos from Fenkenstrain.

post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.speaker: Rologarth
post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.text: I saw him climb up into the Tower to hide it. It doesn't matter - soon the werewolves will come for him, and his experiments will be forever ceased.

post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.player: Do you want the ring back? It is yours after all.

post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.speaker: Rologarth
post-quest-dialogue-lord-rologarth.text: No, you keep it, my friend. Werewolves hunger for the scent of live flesh - I have no need for the ring. I have my castle back, if not my soul.

post-quest-dialogue-dr-fenkenstrain.player: It is all you deserve. Lord Rologarth is master of this castle once more. Let him protect you - if he wants to.
